notes: PSA 7 ng/mL. PI-RADS 5. PSAD 0.07. Prostate volume 95 mL. csPCa 0.79.

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of biopsy-proven prostate cancer with rising PSA trajectory to discuss definitive management options.

This 78-year-old widowed gentleman, an ICT consultant, attends for re-evaluation following a recent prostate biopsy. He resides alone, though his adult son lives nearby, and prefers morning appointments due to reliance on public transport. His PSA has risen steadily over the past year, from 3.4 ng/mL in February 2024 to 7.0 ng/mL in February 2025. He reports no lower urinary tract symptoms, with an IPSS score of 0/35. He is an ex-smoker (39 pack-years, quit in 2008) and consumes approximately 7 units of alcohol weekly. His mobility is limited, restricting him to chair-based exercises only. He recently attended an endocrine appointment for thyroid screening. He reports no bone pain, haematuria, or weight loss.

Per rectum, the prostate is enlarged but symmetrically smooth with no palpable nodules or induration, consistent with a clinical stage cT1c. General examination reveals a cachectic build with a BMI of 18.8, blood pressure of 152/73 mmHg, and a heart rate of 74 bpm. There is no peripheral lymphadenopathy or spinal tenderness.
